hlt.title: Site health
hlt.sub: One line each for customer problems, the server, speed, the site audit, the smoke test and the saved journeys. Green is fine, yellow needs a look, red is wrong, grey has nothing to judge yet.
hlt.noServer: No server reports reach this copy of the shop (a developer machine), so the server, speed and smoke lines stay grey.

problems.notYet: Not recording yet. The privacy-safe problem recorder comes next and fills this line.
problems.urgent: {n} urgent problem open ({open} open in all). Customers are stuck: open it now.
problems.important: {n} important problem open ({open} open in all).
problems.off: The recorder is off ({open} still open).
problems.minor: Only problems that can wait are open ({open}).

server.noReport: No report from the server's health check yet.
server.late: The server's health check is {min} minutes late.
server.worker: The background worker has stopped (no heartbeat).
server.workerNever: The background worker has not started yet.
server.ok: Every service is up and the background worker is alive.

speed.noReport: No speed reading from the server yet.
speed.late: The last speed reading is {min} minutes old.
speed.noAnswer: The home page did not answer the server's check.
speed.slow: The home page took {ms} ms (yellow above {limit} ms).
speed.ok: The home page answered in {ms} ms.

audit.notYet: No checklist audit yet. Start one on AI › Checklist audit.
audit.okAgents: {passed} checklist groups passed, none failed; {agents} wait for the audit agents.

smoke.never: No smoke test has run yet.
smoke.late: The last smoke test is {h} hours old (it runs after every deploy and every night).

journeys.scheduleOff: Not scheduled (off). Press Run now below, or switch the schedule on.
journeys.never: Scheduled; no run yet. The server starts the first one within the hour.
journeys.late: The last run is {h} hours old; it should have run again by now.
journeys.okSkipped: All {journeys} journeys passed ({steps} steps; {skipped} skipped because the shop has nothing to open there yet).

note.k6: First load measurement (k6): 95% of requests within {p95} ms.
note.asked: Run now was pressed; the server starts it within the hour.

card.d: Only how the lines are judged; nothing on the server changes.
card.monitorStaleMinutesHelp: The server checks itself every minute.
card.siteSlowMsHelp: The server's own alert uses its own limit.
card.smokeStaleHoursHelp: It runs after every deploy and every night.

err.STALE: Someone else changed this; it shows their values now.
err.forbidden: You do not have permission to change this.
err.unauthorized: Your sign-in has ended — please sign in again.
err.other: That did not save. Please try again.

hlt.readOnly: You can see these limits; changing them needs the settings permission.

j.d: A customer, the admin, an accountant and the warehouse, walked in a real browser on a phone and a desktop screen. The customer never puts anything in the bag and never orders. Plain browser steps; AI is not needed.
j.asked: Asked. The server starts the run within the hour; this page shows it when it is done.
j.waiting: Waiting for the server to start the run you asked for.
j.noPerm: Running them needs the settings permission.

err.INVALID_INPUT: That did not work. Please try again.
err.forbidden: You do not have permission to do this.
err.unauthorized: Your sign-in has ended — please sign in again.
err.other: That did not work. Please try again.

jcard.d: The server checks every hour and starts a run when one is due. Off as it ships.
jcard.enabledHelp: Off: they run only when someone presses Run now.
jcard.keepRunsHelp: Older runs are removed from the server.
jcard.readOnly: You can see the schedule; changing it needs the settings permission.

ucard.d: After every step of the saved journeys, on the phone and the desktop screen, the page is also measured the way the device gate measures it before every release. Each finding fails its step.
ucard.enabled: Check how the pages look in every run
ucard.enabledHelp: Off: the journeys only check that every page opens and works.
ucard.layoutHelp: Wider than the screen, sideways scrolling, something sticking out, a squeezed tab.
ucard.textHelp: Text cut short; on the phone also form text under 16 px (the iPhone zooms in).
ucard.tapsHelp: Too small for a finger on the phone, two on top of each other, or covered by something.

spd.title: Speed
spd.sub: How fast the shop is for real visitors and in the monthly check on a phone over 4G, against your targets.

kpi.inp: Real visitors: response to a tap (INP, phone)

spd.labD: The home, a category and a product page on a phone over slow 4G, and an admin page on a desktop, measured from the server.
spd.labNone: No check yet. It runs on the 2nd of each month, or press Measure now.
spd.asked: Asked. The server measures within the hour; this page shows it when it is done.
spd.waiting: Waiting for the server to measure.
spd.noPerm: Measuring now needs the settings permission.

err.INVALID_INPUT: That did not work. Please try again.
err.forbidden: You do not have permission to do this.
err.unauthorized: Your sign-in has ended — please sign in again.
err.other: That did not work. Please try again.

spd.realD: The 75th percentile of the last {days} days: three in four visits were at least this fast. From {n} visits.
spd.realNone: No real visitor readings in the last {days} days yet.
spd.monthsD: Real visitors on a phone (75th percentile) and that month's check. Red misses the target.
spd.targetsD: The targets are kept with the speed settings on Website › SEO: loading {lcp}, layout shift {cls}, tap response {inp}, server answer {ttfb}, category page weight {kb}, admin load {admin}.

card.d: How many months the month-by-month table shows.
card.readOnly: You can see this; changing it needs the settings permission.

smk.title: Smoke runs
smk.sub: After every deploy and every night a real browser opens every built page on a phone and a desktop. Here is the newest run, page by page.

kpi.pagesFoot: {views} page views on a phone and a desktop

smk.putBack: A page failed after this deploy, so the previous version was put back automatically. Fix it before anything new.
smk.problemsMore: and {n} more in the list below
smk.none: No smoke run is kept on the server yet. It runs after every deploy and every night; this page fills after the next one.
smk.noneFailed: No page failed in this run.
smk.noRows: This run is from before the page-by-page list; the next run fills it. Its summary is above.
smk.adminShots: Pictures of admin pages are hidden for you: they can show customers' names. Seeing them needs the permission health.smoke.shots (the owner adds it to a role).

hst.title: Run history
hst.sub: Every smoke test and saved-journeys run, with what passed and what failed. Old runs stay for comparison.
hst.none: No run kept yet. The smoke test runs after every deploy and every night; the saved journeys on their schedule or with Run now.
hst.noneFiltered: No run matches what you chose.
hst.caught: {n} runs were added from the server's files just now.

run.title: {tool} · {when}
run.fixedD: These failed in the run before and not in this one.
run.firstNote: This is the first run of this kind in the history, so there is nothing to compare with yet.

hst.fixNone: No fix proposed. A fix needs the owner's OK on Fixes to approve.

fixStatus.none: No fix on the finding now.
fixStatus.proposed: The fix waits for a decision.
fixStatus.approved: Approved: waiting to be fixed on the test server and checked again.
fixStatus.expired: Expired: nobody decided in time; nothing was changed.
fixStatus.fixed: Fixed: the same check passed again.
fixStatus.rolled-back: Rolled back: the check got worse, so the fix was undone.

sum.by: Written by rules from this run and the one before it; AI is not needed for it.
sum.headFailed: Failed: {urgent} urgent, {important} important, {canWait} that can wait.
sum.headStuck: The test itself did not run through.
sum.recovered: Fixed since the run before: that one failed, this one passed.
sum.passedWithNotes: {n} small notes were kept, but none stopped the run.
sum.stuck: Nothing is known about the shop from this run (for example the server was busy or the test timed out). Look at the next run.
sum.down: Nearly every page failed ({failed} of {total}): the site or the server was probably down or unreachable. Check Server first.
sum.serverErrors: {n} pages answered with a server error (5xx): the shop's server had a problem there.
sum.rolledBack: The new version {sha} was rolled back by itself because this test failed.
sum.newVersion: The run before passed and this one runs a new version ({sha}): the failure probably came with that version.
sum.money: {n} problems are on the bag or checkout: customers may not be able to order. Look at these first.
sum.adminOnly: Only admin pages failed: customers are not affected.
sum.shopOnly: Only shop pages failed: customers may see it.
sum.oneScreen: It fails only on the {screen}: probably the layout for that screen.
sum.looksOnly: Everything still works; it only looks wrong (cut text, small buttons and the like).
sum.streak: This test has failed {n} times in a row: the problem is not going away by itself.
sum.same: The same problems as the run before: nothing new broke.
sum.few: Problems on {pages} pages; see the list below.

alerts.d: A line to you on Telegram when the smoke test or the saved journeys fail, again while it keeps failing, and one when it passes again. It uses the bot on Keys & connections; until that is connected, the lines are only kept in the server's alert log. The server reads a change within a few minutes.
alerts.readOnly: Only someone who can change settings can change this.
alerts.enabled: Send a line when a test fails
alerts.enabledHelp: Off: nothing is sent; the runs are still kept here.
alerts.smokeHelp: After every deploy and every night.
alerts.journeysHelp: On their own schedule, or when someone presses "Run now".
alerts.repeatHours: While it keeps failing, again at most every (hours)
alerts.repeatHoursHelp: From 1 to 168 (a week). The line says how long it has been failing.
alerts.recovered: A line when it passes again
alerts.recoveredHelp: Only after a line said it failed.
alerts.toldFailingQuiet: {tool}: failing since {since}; no line sent (switched off).

fxg.title: Fixes to approve
fxg.sub: Agents' proposed fixes and new skills. Nothing changes without your OK.
fxg.rule: Nothing changes without your OK. An agent proposes a fix → you approve it → it is fixed on the test server first → the same check runs again → only then it goes live, and if anything gets worse it is rolled back. An approved new skill is ready but stays switched off until it is turned on in the skill library.
fxg.off: Agents may not propose anything now (the switch below is off), so nothing new will wait here.

kpi.expire: an undecided one expires after {days} days

fixStatus.none: No fix on the finding now.
fixStatus.proposed: The fix waits for a decision.
fixStatus.approved: Approved: waiting to be fixed on the test server and checked again.
fixStatus.expired: Expired: nobody decided in time; nothing was changed.
fixStatus.fixed: Fixed: the same check passed again.
fixStatus.rolled-back: Rolled back: the check got worse, so the fix was undone.

fxg.ownNote: You proposed this one, so someone else has to decide it.
fxg.cannotDecide: Only the owner (or someone allowed to approve fixes) can decide this.
fxg.openRun: Open the run this came from

approveD.title: Approve this proposal?
approveD.fix1: The fix is allowed to run, on the test server first.
approveD.fix2: The same check runs again; only if it passes does the fix go live.
approveD.fix3: If anything gets worse, it is rolled back by itself.
approveD.skill1: This version becomes the skill's current version.
approveD.skill2: A new skill stays switched off until it is turned on in the skill library.

rejectD.title: Reject this proposal?
rejectD.fix1: Nothing is changed on the site.
rejectD.fix2: The finding stays open; an agent can propose a different fix.
rejectD.skill1: The skill version is kept, but it is not used.
rejectD.skill2: An agent can propose a better version later.

err.DECIDED: Someone already decided this one. The list is fresh now.
err.NOT_FOUND: This proposal is no longer here. The list is fresh now.
err.OWN_PROPOSAL: You cannot decide your own proposal.
err.forbidden: You are not allowed to decide proposals.

none.waiting: Nothing is waiting for your OK.

card.d: Whether agents may propose fixes and new skills at all, and when an undecided proposal expires. Approving is always a person's step.
card.readOnly: Only someone who can change settings can change this.
card.proposals: Agents may propose fixes and new skills
card.proposalsHelp: Off: nothing is proposed and nothing waits. On: every proposal waits here for your OK.
card.expireDays: Days before an undecided proposal expires
card.expireDaysHelp: 0 = never. An expired one changes nothing and can be proposed again.

aud.title: Checklist audit
aud.sub: The full e-commerce checklist, group by group, and the runner that checks it on the live preview.
aud.rule: An audit only checks and reports. Any fix waits for your OK on Fixes to approve; nothing is changed by itself.
aud.off: The schedule is off. An audit runs only when someone presses "Run now".
aud.agentsMock: The audit agents (AI) are a practice copy until the AI key is on Keys & connections: groups that no script covers wait for them.

run.asked: Asked. The server starts the audit within the hour.
run.waiting: Asked. The server starts the audit within the hour.
run.noPerm: Only someone who can change settings can start an audit.

card.d: When the checklist is audited, which groups, how many agents, and whether the report goes to your Telegram. The server reads a change within a few minutes.
card.readOnly: Only someone who can change settings can change this.
card.enabledHelp: Off: only "Run now" starts an audit.
card.hourHelp: A quiet hour is best; an audit takes about half an hour.
card.agentsHelp: How many agents judge the points no script covers. A practice copy until the AI key is there.
card.telegramHelp: The result and the problem list, after every audit.
